IEEE 754 floating point

Source: R/fpa.R
z3_fp.Rd

Z3's floating point theory models IEEE 754 binary formats exactly, including rounding, signed zeros, infinities and NaN. A format has ebits exponent bits and sbits significand bits (counting the hidden bit): z3_fp_sort(ctx, 11, 53) is double precision, the format of R's numbers. The standard formats also have names: z3_fp_sort(ctx, "half"), "single", "double" and "quadruple", or by width z3_fp_sort(ctx, 16), 32, 64 and 128, the same as z3_fp16_sort(), z3_fp32_sort(), z3_fp64_sort() and z3_fp128_sort().

Usage

z3_fp_sort(ctx, ebits, sbits)

z3_fp16_sort(ctx)

z3_fp32_sort(ctx)

z3_fp64_sort(ctx)

z3_fp128_sort(ctx)

z3_rounding_sort(ctx)

z3_fp_sort_info(x)

z3_fp(ctx, name, sort)

z3_fp_val(ctx, x, sort, rounding = NULL)

z3_rounding(
  ctx,
  mode = c("RNE", "RNA", "RTP", "RTN", "RTZ", "roundNearestTiesToEven",
    "roundNearestTiesToAway", "roundTowardPositive", "roundTowardNegative",
    "roundTowardZero")
)

z3_fp_nan(sort)

z3_fp_inf(sort, negative = FALSE)

z3_fp_zero(sort, negative = FALSE)

z3_fp_from_bits(sign, exponent, significand)

z3_fp_add(rounding, x, y)

z3_fp_sub(rounding, x, y)

z3_fp_mul(rounding, x, y)

z3_fp_div(rounding, x, y)

z3_fp_fma(rounding, x, y, z)

z3_fp_sqrt(rounding, x)

z3_fp_round_to_integral(rounding, x)

z3_fp_rem(x, y)

z3_fp_min(x, y)

z3_fp_max(x, y)

z3_fp_abs(x)

z3_fp_neg(x)

z3_fp_eq(x, y)

z3_fp_lt(x, y)

z3_fp_leq(x, y)

z3_fp_gt(x, y)

z3_fp_geq(x, y)

z3_fp_is_nan(x)

z3_fp_is_infinite(x)

z3_fp_is_zero(x)

z3_fp_is_normal(x)

z3_fp_is_subnormal(x)

z3_fp_is_negative(x)

z3_fp_is_positive(x)

z3_fp_to_real(x)

z3_fp_to_ieee_bv(x)

z3_fp_to_ubv(rounding, x, size)

z3_fp_to_sbv(rounding, x, size)

z3_fp_to_fp(rounding, x, sort)

z3_fp_from_bv(bv, sort)

z3_fp_from_signed(rounding, bv, sort)

z3_fp_from_unsigned(rounding, bv, sort)

z3_fp_from_real_exp(rounding, exponent, significand, sort)

z3_fp_numeral_parts(x, biased = FALSE, numeric = FALSE)

z3_fp_from_parts(sort, negative, exponent_value, fraction)

Arguments

ctx

A z3_context().

ebits, sbits

Exponent and significand widths. With sbits omitted, ebits names a standard format: "half", "single", "double", "quadruple", or a width 16, 32, 64 or 128.

x, y, z

Floating point expressions or R numbers (any value for z3_fp_to_fp()).

name

Name of a constant.

sort

A floating point sort.

rounding

A rounding mode from z3_rounding().

mode

Rounding mode name, short ("RNE") or SMT-LIB ("roundNearestTiesToEven").

negative

Sign of an infinity or zero.

size

Width of the resulting bit-vector.

bv, sign, exponent, significand

Bit-vector expressions; for z3_fp_from_real_exp(), an Int exponent and a Real significand.

biased

For z3_fp_numeral_parts(): report the biased exponent.

numeric

For z3_fp_numeral_parts(): also give the sign, exponent and fraction as numbers.

exponent_value

Unbiased exponent, a whole number or string.

fraction

The fraction bits of the significand as an integer (without the hidden bit), a whole number or string.

Value

A z3_expr or z3_sort; z3_fp_sort_info() returns the two widths; z3_fp_numeral_parts() a list: class ("normal", "subnormal", "zero", "infinite" or "nan") and negative; significand and exponent as decimal strings for finite values; and for every value but NaN the fields as bit-vectors (sign_bv, exponent_bv, significand_bv). With numeric = TRUE, values other than NaN also have sign (0 or 1), exponent_value and fraction (the fraction bits without the hidden bit, as an integer), each a double while exact (at most 2^53 in magnitude) and a decimal string beyond.

Details

Values. z3_fp(ctx, name, sort) makes a constant. R numbers combined with a floating point expression are converted to its format only when the format represents them exactly; NaN, Inf and -0 are kept. z3_fp_val(ctx, x, sort, rounding) rounds an R number into a format explicitly. z3_fp_nan(), z3_fp_inf() and z3_fp_zero() give the special values. z3_value() converts numerals back to R doubles exactly.

Operators. +, -, *, / and unary - use round-to-nearest, ties-to-even ("RNE"), the rounding of R's own arithmetic; %% is the IEEE remainder. <, <=, >, >= are IEEE comparisons (false when either side is NaN). == and != are structural equality, as for every other sort: NaN == NaN is true and 0 == -0 is false. Use z3_fp_eq() for IEEE equality, where the opposite holds.

Explicit rounding. z3_rounding(ctx, mode) gives a rounding mode: "RNE" (nearest, ties to even), "RNA" (nearest, ties away from zero), "RTP" (toward +Inf), "RTN" (toward -Inf), "RTZ" (toward zero), or by its SMT-LIB name, which z3_value() returns: "roundNearestTiesToEven", "roundNearestTiesToAway", "roundTowardPositive", "roundTowardNegative", "roundTowardZero". z3_fp_add(), z3_fp_sub(), z3_fp_mul(), z3_fp_div(), z3_fp_fma(), z3_fp_sqrt() and z3_fp_round_to_integral() take it as their first argument.

Other operations. z3_fp_rem(), z3_fp_min(), z3_fp_max(), z3_fp_abs() (also abs()), z3_fp_neg(); predicates z3_fp_is_nan(), z3_fp_is_infinite(), z3_fp_is_zero(), z3_fp_is_normal(), z3_fp_is_subnormal(), z3_fp_is_negative(), z3_fp_is_positive(); comparisons z3_fp_lt(), z3_fp_leq(), z3_fp_gt(), z3_fp_geq(), z3_fp_eq().

Conversions. z3_fp_to_fp(rounding, x, sort) converts another format, a Real or an Int; z3_fp_from_bv(bv, sort) reinterprets IEEE bits; z3_fp_from_signed()/z3_fp_from_unsigned() convert a bit-vector integer; z3_fp_from_real_exp(rounding, exponent, significand, sort) rounds significand * 2^exponent from an Int exponent and a Real significand, which may be symbolic; z3_fp_from_bits(sign, exponent, significand) assembles the fields; z3_fp_from_parts() builds a numeral exactly from its sign, unbiased exponent and fraction bits; z3_fp_to_ubv()/z3_fp_to_sbv() round to a bit-vector integer of width size; z3_fp_to_real() gives the exact Real value; z3_fp_to_ieee_bv() the bit pattern. z3_fp_numeral_parts() describes a numeral (class, sign, exponent and significand).

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
D <- z3_fp64_sort(ctx)
z3_fp_sort(ctx, "double") == D
#> [1] TRUE
parts <- z3_fp_numeral_parts(z3_fp_val(ctx, 1.5, D), numeric = TRUE)
parts[c("sign", "exponent_value", "fraction")]
#> $sign
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $exponent_value
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $fraction
#> [1] 2.2518e+15
#> 
z3_value(z3_rounding(ctx, "roundTowardZero"))
#> [1] "roundTowardZero"
x <- z3_fp(ctx, "x", D)
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
# 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3 in double precision, as in R
z3_add(s, x == z3_fp_val(ctx, 0.1, D) + z3_fp_val(ctx, 0.2, D))
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(s), x)) == 0.1 + 0.2
#> [1] TRUE
# A number that is its own successor: Inf
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x + 1 == x, !z3_fp_is_nan(x), x > 0)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(s), x))
#> [1] Inf
